x_vs_y.locator_label: structural canary ORACLE (deterministic upper bound; injection-point-visible signal sourced from the injection ledger; a real detector would reconstruct it from per-agent input-message structure, which requires capturing per-agent input prompts that reflect the post-pruning message set actually sent to the model — a known instrumentation gap)

evidence.note: In 39/39 (100%) of drift traces the dropped upstream message is STILL PRESENT in the target agent's captured llm.input_messages (name match). The content-layer input IS captured, but by the on_chat_model_start callback (fires before _generate, hence before the injector's messages[:]=kept prune) -> the span reflects the PRE-deletion state. The deletion is therefore NOT observable from the trajectory -> Y (ledger-only oracle).

Constant-Synthesizer.note: always blame Recommendation_Synthesizer; = fraction of ctxdrift cases rooted at Synthesizer (12/36, scenario(s): ctxdrift_synth_from_prod)

structural_locator.label: structural canary ORACLE (deterministic upper bound; injection-point-visible signal sourced from the injection ledger; a real detector would reconstruct it from per-agent input-message structure, which requires capturing per-agent input prompts that reflect the post-pruning message set actually sent to the model — a known instrumentation gap)

observable_vs_oracle.note: Per-case source split. observed_detector = a GENUINE method: reads the post-pruning received-message names the injector now emits into the trajectory (span `agentfault.resolved_input`, attr `agentfault.resolved_input.msg_names`) and applies the chaosgraph AllRequiredNodesVisited set-diff (missing = expected_upstream - received). ledger_oracle = the upper-bound fallback used when that attribute is ABSENT (old / un-recollected data). The two numbers are NOT merged. On THIS dataset the attribute is present in 36/36 case(s) and absent in 0/36 — so the observable detector carries every case and the oracle fallback is empty.

observable_detector.label: GENUINE observable detector (post-pruning received-msg set-diff; chaosgraph AllRequiredNodesVisited shape)

oracle_fallback.label: ledger-sourced ORACLE (upper bound; attribute absent -> fallback)

convlen_anomaly_vs_clean_carrier.note: per-agent |Δ conv_<A>_text_len| vs same-carrier normal case; seed-avg tie-break; OUTPUT-content feature. NOT a dependable locator: wildly scenario-unstable (by scenario: 0.833 `ctxdrift_ub_from_seq`, 0.417 `ctxdrift_prod_from_ub`, 0.000 `ctxdrift_synth_from_prod`; spread 0.833) — it tracks which agent emits the most variable free text, not the drop (the Synthesizer's templated tool-call output barely changes, hence 0.000 on `ctxdrift_synth_from_prod`). The overall 0.417 is carried by `ctxdrift_ub_from_seq` (0.833); under group-aware CV the same feature set collapses (Tier-A RF-content 0.000).

tierA_quoted_source.note: Hit@1 column parsed at runtime from the Tier-A BASELINE_RESULTS.md table; NOT hardcoded. If parsing fails these read 'UNAVAILABLE (Tier-A parse FAILED — see stderr)' rather than a stale constant.

silent_wrong_caveat: silent_wrong n=9/36 context_drift cases (run_ids: `ctxdrift_ub_from_seq__r3`, `ctxdrift_ub_from_seq__r8`, `ctxdrift_prod_from_ub__r3`, `ctxdrift_prod_from_ub__r4`, `ctxdrift_prod_from_ub__r8`, `ctxdrift_synth_from_prod__r3`, `ctxdrift_synth_from_prod__r6`, `ctxdrift_synth_from_prod__r7`, `ctxdrift_synth_from_prod__r8`) -> n=9 is too small for statistics; read it as a COUNT, not a rate (a binomial interval at n=9 spans most of [0,1]). The per-stratum Hit@1 is descriptive only.

content_track_consolidation.structured_families: Tier-A contract oracle Hit@1=1.000 on wrong_item_pick & 1.000 on format_violation (deterministic content locatable).

content_track_consolidation.context_drift: NOT content-locatable from OUTPUT/infra features (Tier-A RF-content 0.000, RF-infra 0.228, Trivial-corrected 0.028 vs random floor 0.250); only the input-structure canary (this script) catches it.
